body:
The session was test-only. It added two unit tests to viola-hyprland, the crate that holds viola's one Hyprland seam. Together they pin the seam's two MAX_FRAME size bounds at the exact frame.
The hyprctl read test runs the crate's own planted hyprctl stub. A reply of exactly MAX_FRAME bytes is read, and one byte more is refused as oversize.
The dispatch parse test feeds exactly MAX_FRAME bytes, which pass the size check and are then refused. One byte more is refused as oversize.
No product line changed, no caller changed, and no public API, dependency, schema, config, error word or output text was added or retired.
Two remove-the-guard controls showed that each new test fails when its bound is removed. The crate's test count went from 82 to 84. The gates and CI were green.

body_fields.what: the Hyprland seam's hyprctl reader, the bounded read that drains a hyprctl reply and refuses one past MAX_FRAME as oversize; only its unit tests changed
the Hyprland seam's reply parser, the bounded parse of hyprctl clients and dispatch replies that refuses one past MAX_FRAME as oversize; only its unit tests changed

Indirect: the rules on zero flakiness, no retries, and a CI test gate with no skips. The read test spawns a planted hyprctl stub within its deadline, and the gates were green with 0 skipped.

The session added two unit tests to viola-hyprland, test-only, and changed no product line, no caller and no public API.
One test pins the hyprctl read's frame bound at the exact frame: a reply of exactly MAX_FRAME bytes reads as a parsed clients reply, one byte more reads as the oversize seam error with an oversize process-log detail.
The other pins the dispatch reply's frame bound at the exact frame: exactly MAX_FRAME bytes passes the size check and reads as refused, one byte more reads as oversize.
The read test drives the crate's own planted hyprctl stub, not the root fake agent, so the crate's own tests can kill a mutant of the bound; remove-the-guard controls on both bounds held.
No dependency, schema, config, crate, name, gate or CI surface moved; no capability was claimed or retired; no MAX_FRAME value changed.

body: The one external read cap and the shared MAX_FRAME cap (decision max-frame-cap, max-frame-shared-cap, reads-capped-at-max-frame, request-size-limits): the hyprctl reply read and the dispatch reply parse are now proven at exactly MAX_FRAME accepted and MAX_FRAME plus one refused; the cap value itself did not move.

Bounded readers (decision bounded-readers-census, bounded-external-readers): the hyprctl reply reader stays a bounded reader; its bound is now witnessed by a test that drives the read's own drain past its cap, not only by a parse test.

Child output bounded and tolerant (decision child-output-bounded, child-output-tolerant, child-output-tolerant-unknown): the hyprctl child's stdout bound is the one pinned; over-limit output is refused whole as oversize, never truncated.
The hyprctl child deadline (decision hyprctl-read-deadline): the read's cap sits in the same bounded read as the deadline, whose own test is unchanged; no deadline value moved.
Hyprland reply text dropped at the parse (decision hyprland-reply-text-dropped): an exactly-MAX_FRAME dispatch reply that is not the success text reads as a closed refusal, carrying no reply text.

Mutation testing at the epoch audit (decision mutation-testing-at-audit): the two Hyprland MAX_FRAME size-check mutants are now killed by the crate's own unit tests, since the boundary audit runs only the mutated package's tests.

MAX_FRAME checked against data and its revisit signal (decision max-frame-checked-against-ledger, max-frame-revisit-signal): an exactly-MAX_FRAME Hyprland reply is accepted, so the cap's edge is measured for this seam; no ledger value moved.
The process log line for a refused hyprctl read (the oversize detail after process-start and process-exit) is the value the test asserts; no row's code word changed.

The read test plants a real hyprctl stub executable on the crate's own stub helper, each in its own tempdir, both planted before either spawns: a reply of exactly MAX_FRAME bytes reads an empty clients reply with process-start and process-exit lines and no parse-rejected; one byte more reads Oversize with a parse-rejected detail oversize.
